unmapped: Each arm has a deterministic cost c_i known a priori
Subsidy factor alpha known to the learner; target arm is the cheapest arm with mean >= (1-alpha) max mean
Performance measured by two regrets: quality regret E[sum max{(1-alpha)mu_{m*} - mu_{pi_t},0}] and cost regret E[sum max{c_{pi_t} - c_{i*},0}]; results bound their sum
settings.definition_quote: in every round $t \in [T]$ the agent chooses an arm $i \in [K]$ and realizes a reward $r_{t},$ sampled independently from a fixed, but unknown distribution $\mathcal{F}_i$ with mean $\mu_i$ ... and incurs a cost $c_{i}$ ..., which is known a priori. ... we allow the agent to be agnostic between arms, whose expected reward is greater than $1- \alpha$ fraction of the highest expected reward, for a fixed and known value of $\alpha$

conditions: Applies to the CS-TS algorithm with Gaussian prior/posterior
Hard instance has deterministic rewards (unknown to agent)

source.label: thm::ts-lin-reg
source.quote: For any given $K, \alpha, T$  there exists an instance $\phi$ of problem such that $\qreg_{{\sf \consTS }}(T,\alpha,\phi) + \creg_{{\sf \consTS }}(T,\alpha,\phi)$  is $\Omega\left(T\right)$.

results.notes: Algorithm-specific lower bound for CS-TS (sum of quality and cost regret). Quantity is sum of quality and cost regret, recorded as 'other'.

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: For any given $\alpha, K, T$ and (possibly randomized) policy $\pi$, there exists an instance $\phi$ of problem \eqref{eq:regret} with $K+1$ arms such that $    \qreg_\pi(T, \alpha, \phi) + \creg_\pi(T,\alpha,\phi) $ is  $ \Omega\left((1-\alpha)^2 K^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{\frac{2}{3}}\right)$ when $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1$ and  $1 \leq K \leq T$.

results.notes: Bound on sum of quality and cost regret. Paper notes it remains valid with unknown costs.

symbols.p: mean reward of the cheap arm 0 in the hard instance family

conditions: instance from the family Phi_{0,p,eps} of K+1 Bernoulli arms

source.label: lem:alpha_0_neat
source.quote: For any given $p, K, T$ and any (possibly randomized) policy $\pi$, there exists an instance $\phi$ (from the family $\cIzero$) such that $\qreg_{\pi}(T, 0,\phi) + \creg_{\pi}(T, 0,\phi)$ is $\Omega\left( pK^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{\frac{2}{3}} \right)$ when $0 < p \leq 1/2$ and $1 \leq  K \leq T$.

results.notes: Special case alpha=0 used in proof of Theorem 2.

source.label: thm:explore_first_regret
source.quote: For an instance $\phi$ with $K$ arms, when  the number of exploration pulls of each arm $ \tau = (T/K)^{2/3}$, then the sum of cost and quality regret incurred by \mainALG \  (Algorithm \ref{alg:explore_first}) on any instance $\phi$ i.e. $\qreg_{\mainALG}(T, \alpha,  \phi) + \creg_{\mainALG}(T, \alpha, \phi)$ is $O(K^{1/3}T^{2/3}\sqrt{\log{T}})$.

results.notes: Sum of quality and cost regret. Paper states (informally) it also holds for a modified algorithm with unknown random costs in [0,1].

symbols.delta_c: consistency constant: |c_i - c_j| <= delta_c |mu_i - mu_j| for all arms i, j

conditions: |c_i - c_j| <= delta_c |mu_i - mu_j| for all i, j (delta_c possibly unknown)

source.label: thm:cost_quality_consistent
source.quote: If for an instance $\phi$ with $K$ arms,  $|c_i - c_j| \leq \delta |\mu_i - \mu_j| \ \forall i, j \in [K]$ and any (possibly unknown) $\delta >0$, then $\qreg_{\consUCB}(T, \alpha,  \phi) + \creg_{\consUCB}(T, \alpha, \phi)$ is $O((1+\delta) \sqrt{KT \log{T}})$.

results.notes: Sum of quality and cost regret under cost-quality consistency.
